spec_match.rationale: Implements the explainer's collection pattern faithfully: a real pagehide listener that calls getSpeculations(), preserves event.persisted for the BFCache case, and previews the exact fetch(…, {keepalive:true}) POST — with the payload built from the real API when present.

interactive.rationale: A run-the-handler-now button executes the genuine handler on demand, a second button renders the exact keepalive call with real byte counts, and the handler is also truly registered on pagehide.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises firing the exact handler on demand and inspecting the JSON payload that would be beaconed; both are delivered, with the persisted flag included on real pagehide firings.

edge_cases.rationale: Method-absent, throwing calls, and BFCache persistence are all handled honestly, but the beacon itself is never actually sent — the /collect server route is an acknowledged TODO, so the keepalive-outlives-the-page behaviour that motivates the pattern is demonstrated only as a preview.

references.rationale: See-also cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/5118840377835520 plus the three sibling concepts.

conformance.rationale: The suite's instance-method and shape assertions cover the read this handler performs; failures in this Chromium 141 session are only the expected absent experimental method.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CLI/CDP (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): DOM shows the honest 'unavailable (payload will be empty)' API state and registered-handler status; zero console errors, no unintended failed requests; the two buttons and a real pagehide/BFCache transition could not be driven non-interactively.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts the API state, every payload build with live/pagehide context, and beacon previews with byte counts.

design_system.rationale: Tokenised colours throughout, but the TODO note's strong text uses --accent-amber on --bg-paper at 0.72rem (~3.3:1), visible by default and under the AA 4.5:1 bar; the unavailable state itself is AA-clean rose.

accessibility.rationale: aria-live payload pane, native focus-visible buttons, and all states (API availability, payload source, unfired-request explanation) expressed as text.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360×740 DPR3 measures 0px horizontal overflow (payload pane wraps and scrolls internally); desktop 1280×800 clean; only the environmental Google Fonts request fails.

openQuestions.title: Wire the /v150/speculative-load-measurement/collect route in server.ts and fire the real beacon
openQuestions.detail: The page's own TODO says it: the demo previews but never sends the keepalive POST because the collect route (respond 204) is unwired. Since the routine is fenced out of server.ts, queue this as a manual task; once wired, actually fire fetch(COLLECT, {keepalive:true}) from the handler, show the response status in the fire log, and demonstrate the request surviving a real navigation away. That upgrades edge_cases to a full pass and matches invariant 7's server-side-route guidance for HTTP-flavoured behaviours.

openQuestions.title: Fix the TODO note's amber contrast
openQuestions.detail: The todo-note strong text is --accent-amber #b87b00 on --bg-paper at 0.72rem, ~3.3:1 against the AA 4.5:1 requirement, and it renders by default for every visitor. A darker amber (or charcoal text with an amber border only) clears it.

openQuestions.title: Record a real pagehide firing with event.persisted context
openQuestions.detail: The handler's on-pagehide path (including persisted=true BFCache entry) was not observable headlessly. In an interactive session, navigate away and back-forward to capture the payload with pagehidePersisted set both ways.

summary: An honest implementation of the explainer's beacon pattern with a genuinely registered pagehide handler, real payload building, BFCache awareness, and a transparent unwired-route disclosure instead of a dead request. Verified with headless Chromium 141 via CLI/CDP (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable in this environment): truthful unavailable state, clean console, no unintended failed requests, no overflow on either class. Main follow-up: wire the collect route server-side (manual task) so the keepalive beacon can actually fire, plus the amber contrast fix and a real pagehide capture.
